messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want distance traveled in time t given initial velocity v and launch angle theta. This is a projectile motion problem. The distance traveled horizontally is v * cos(theta) * t. The vertical distance is v * sin(theta) * t - 0.5 * g * t^2. But the question: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" Might be asking for range? But they mention time t. So maybe they want horizontal distance traveled in time t: x = v * cos(theta) * t. If they want total distance traveled (arc length), that's more complex. But likely they want horizontal displacement. They might want to use the projectile range formula: R = (v^2 * sin(2θ)) / g. But that gives total range until landing. But they mention time t. So we can compute horizontal distance: d = v * cos(theta) * t. If they want vertical displacement: y = v * sin(theta) * t - 0.5 * g * t^2. So answer: horizontal distance = v * cos(theta) * t.
